title: My posture nearly killed me. Here's why...
description:
Blueprint is a public science experiment to determine whether it’s possible to stay the same biological age. This requires slowing down aging processes as much as possible and then reversing the aging that has happened. Currently my speed of aging is .76 (DunedinPACE). That means for every 365 days each year, I age 277 days. My goal is to remain the same age biologically for every 365 days that pass.  

I openly share (for free!) my diet, exercise and other protocols so that others can benefit and try to improve upon what I’m doing. I also openly share my health data as data is better than human opinion at guiding decision making. You can find everything here: https://blueprint.bryanjohnson.co/ 

On the surface, Blueprint may seem like something about health, wellness and aging. To me, it’s a philosophy. 

Blueprint was born when years ago I would overeat every night as a result of the stress of everyday life: being a startup entrepreneur, a father to three young kids, leaving a religion I was born into, chronic depression etc.. Every night, at 7 PM, there was nothing I could do to stop myself from committing this self-harm of overeating. This was rapidly degrading my health and wellness and speeding up my pace of aging. Eventually, I playfully fired ‘Evening Bryan’, and revoked his decision-making authority from 7 PM - 10 PM every night. 

I imagine a future where we would not accept self-harm as the norm. The idea of systematically and reliably avoiding self-harm may be one of the most important goals of the 21st century. How silly is it that we do things, individually and collectively that harm our self-interests? How odd is it that we are so normalized to it that we even cheer it on? 

Our best selves, and a positive shared future, may start with this simple principle. Blueprint is the plan for that.

for preventative cancer screening I found that I had a jugular vein stenosis so we had these two big veins on the side of our necks they are the highways for blood so the MRI showed that I had severe stenosis severe cloggage and it was causing intracranial pressures my team and I went on this kind of Code Red Alert we didn't know how serious it was like was I going to have a seizure was I going to have a stroke like at any moment how bad was it and so we did a bunch of additional measurements I have an ultrasound machine at the house in the clinic we do ultrasound measurements looking at actual flow we did more MRIs

we did an mrv looking at all the vasculature of my upper chest neck and head we did two different tests looking in my eye your eyes have an insight into intracranial pressure for your brain so anyways I did all this testing I started going to medications and we became expert at this given thing and meanwhile I'm doing PT every day to try to correct my posture so I now I'm obsessed with posture because it so dramatically affects the flow but it's really I guess like this is not a part of normal care like this has existed my whole life no one has ever found it
it's like why don't we know more about these things why aren't these standard routine things for all of us
